result.title: When Does Exercise-Specific Joint Selection Help? An Audit of Evaluation and Control Design
result.comment: Exploratory offline audit of subject-disjoint skeleton-based exercise correctness evaluation; 5 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables
result.summary: Exercise-specific joint selection can improve skeleton-based correctness classification, but what does that gain establish? We audit 1,057 repetitions from ten REHAB24-6 subjects, separating evaluation aggregation, subset structure, and temporal representation. The manual-subset kNN gain changes from 0.055 for pooled out-of-fold AUROC to 0.020 for equal-weight within-person AUROC; both paired intervals include zero. Among 1,000 dimension-matched random maps, 14 match or exceed the manual pooled result, versus 145 when bilateral structure and trunk inclusion are also matched. RBF-SVM retains a positive within-person gain, whereas logistic regression and a random-convolution comparator have negative point gains under that estimand. Sequence-order and paired-seed controls further qualify the interpretation. This exploratory audit shows why joint-selection claims require explicit estimands and structurally appropriate controls; it does not establish a new algorithm or clinical benefit.

AI.brief_summary: 该文对 10 名受试者、1,057 次重复动作的骨架动作正确性分类做离线审计，分解评估聚合方式、子集结构与时间表示三类因素，并用手工关节子集与 1,000 个维度匹配随机映射对照，说明关节选择增益高度依赖估计目标与结构性控制。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽非 VLM/LVR 工作，但其关于估计目标、聚合口径与匹配结构化随机基线的方法，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 子空间或视觉证据选择增益是否被统计口径放大。
